title: Environmental redox conditions and strain variation define phenazine-mediated antagonism in co-infecting bacteria
experiments_summary: Wild Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Pa) strains (145.1, 191.1, 193.1) were identified from mouse gut samples via MALDI-TOF and whole-genome sequencing. Co-culture and filter-sterilized spent media assays in LB broth and M9-cas were used to assess contact-independent restriction of Klebsiella pneumoniae (Kp) KPPR1 growth by Pa strains (PAO1, PA14, wild isolates) and control organisms (E. coli MG1655, Kp 13F11). Growth curves and area-under-curve analyses measured strain-specific growth dynamics. BioLog PM1/PM2 carbon source utilization arrays assessed metabolic niche overlap. Nutrient supplementation experiments (casamino acids, glucose) tested whether restoration of Kp growth was possible in Pa-spent media. A PA14 transposon library screen (5,708 mutants) using a GFP-expressing KPPR1 reporter identified candidate genes required for Kp restriction; 18 candidates were validated by co-culture and spent media assays. Markerless deletion mutants (ΔrhlR, ΔrhlI, ΔphzA-G1/2, ΔphzH, ΔphzM, ΔphzS, ΔphzHMS) were tested in co-culture and spent media assays in LB and M9-cas to map the phenazine biosynthesis pathway's role in Kp restriction. A heterologous E. coli expression system constitutively producing PCA, PYR (5MPCA via spontaneous phzS frameshift), or PYO was used to test sufficiency of individual phenazines. High-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-QTOF) confirmed phenazine identity in spent media. MIC and MBC assays for PYO, PCA, 1-HP, and PYR were conducted in fresh LB and PA14ΔphzA-G spent media under aerobic and anaerobic conditions; nitrate supplementation tested anaerobic respiration dependency. Checkerboard assays assessed PYO-PYR additivity/synergy. Phenazine concentrations were estimated spectrophotometrically (Abs695 for PYO, Abs500 for PYR) from Pa spent media. Clinical isolate screens included 198 Kp isolates grown in PA14 spent media, 41 Kp isolates grown in phenazine-expressing E. coli spent media, and 194 Pa isolates competed against KPPR1-GFP to assess strain-dependent restriction; phenazine production was correlated with restriction phenotype. Specificity was tested against K. oxytoca, uropathogenic E. coli, and Enterococcus faecalis using the heterologous expression system. Ex vivo competition assays were performed anaerobically in mouse large intestinal contents and aerobically in murine bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and bladder homogenate using WT PA14 and PA14ΔphzA-G. An in vivo gut colonization model used ampicillin-pretreated C57Bl6/J mice sequentially gavaged with Pa 191.1 and KPPR1, with fecal and cecal CFU quantification on selective media. Reducing agent (DTT) titration into PYR-containing spent media tested redox dependence of PYR bactericidal activity. All in vitro data were analyzed by two-tailed t-test or ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc correction on log10-transformed values.
